Both flow readers describe the declared grouping-by-part pattern in book order with Veldmark and the index last, and mark no section's position unclear. Both noted the layout is announced at the end of p01 and again in p02 (reader-flow-a item 1, reader-flow-b item 10) but both said it did not lose them; this is the spec's declared roadmap-then-elaboration design and is not counted as a material point.

results.draft_locus: Reading the Book table (Vanity Liquidity row)
results.quote: | **Vanity Liquidity** | The marketplace measures listings and visits instead of matches
results.finding: Both flow readers took the failure-pattern rows to follow the parts and had to stop when Vanity Liquidity (Part I repair), Billing by Guesswork (Part VI) and Set-and-Forget AI (Part VII) come after the Part VIII patterns; nothing on the page states the order. Reader A: 'on a first pass it looks almost chapter-ordered and then breaks.' Fix in the draft: state in p04 that the rows follow where-listing-systems-go-wrong's order, or order them by repair part.

results.draft_locus: Part III — Supply table (Lead ledger row)
results.quote: | **Lead ledger** | One store of deduplicated leads across channels
results.finding: Both flow readers met the lead ledger and lead management in Part III before Lead is defined in Part VI and had to jump ahead or check that the forward reference was deliberate, despite the p07 pointer ('the professional's side of the lead that Part VI defines'). Reader A: 'I had to jump ahead to the Money section to anchor it.' The spec's grouping puts these rows in Part III; a row-level cross-reference (e.g. 'see Lead, Part VI') fixes it in the draft without reordering.

results.draft_locus: Part VIII — Leadership table (Decision rights / decision record row)
results.quote: | **Decision rights / decision record** | Who may decide what
results.finding: Both flow readers found names defined twice with different meanings and no note in the rows (decision record in Parts V and VIII, policy in Parts II and V, chargeback in Parts VI and VIII), against KEY POINTS' 'One term, one meaning, one owning chapter'; both re-read at the second 'decision record'. The index disambiguates but the rows do not. Fix in the draft: a short 'not the same as' note in each clashing row.

Both flow readers followed index entries to terms no row defines: 'Cost per lead' (no row; nearest are Pay per lead and 'cost per contact') and the alias '(aspect)' in 'Instance attribute (aspect)' / 'Product attribute (aspect)', which the Part II row never uses. This breaks p14's promise that the index lists 'every row term, abbreviation and common alias defined above'. Fix the entries or the rows.

Reader A paused at platform-technical rows (Aggregate, Domain event, Anti-corruption layer, External system of record) in the 'business vocabulary' section, and at 'system of record' used four parts before Listing system of record is defined. Reported by one reader only.
